name: Stack
description: A buff or debuff that can be increased in count (up to a cap) under certain circumstances; potency is usually multiplied by the number of stacks, and some stacks are counters that build toward a different, triggerable effect (e.g. Caitlyn's Headshot).

name: Stack duration refresh
description: Stacking effects with durations refresh per instance; all stacks reset to the most recent application's full duration, and when the effect times out all stacks expire at once (a few exceptions, e.g. Nautilus' Titan's Wrath, expire in intervals or per-stack).

name: Maximum stacks
description: A stacking effect has a predetermined maximum number of stacks; at the cap, further applications no longer increase the count (e.g. Rev'd up stacks up to 3, Concussive Blows up to 4, Hemorrhage up to 5).

name: Stack consumption / threshold trigger
description: Stacks that are consumed or spent to power a trigger: expending all stacks to empower the next ability (Rengar Ferocity, Renekton Rage), consuming stacks to apply a bonus effect (Blade of the Ruined King at 3 stacks), or gating an empowered state until a counter is full.

name: Effect stacking
description: Whether an effect applied several times to the same unit stacks or not: different effects always stack with each other; a non-stacking effect only resets its duration on reapplication; auras do not stack with themselves (a unit affected by two identical auras receives the effect once), with exceptions for aura user-vs-recipient effects.

name: Additive stacking
description: Multiple sources of the same statistic combine by simple addition (e.g. two +100 health items grant +200 health); applies to most stats including mana, health, AD, AP, armor, attack speed bonuses, lifesteal and flat penetration.

name: Multiplicative stacking
description: Sources combine by multiplying the underlying factors (10% + 10% damage reduction = 0.9 x 0.9 = 19% total reduction); applies to percent penetration, cripples, slow resist and to damage amplifiers vs damage reductions.

name: Buff
description: A status effect that gives a champion or minion a beneficial boost; most buffs are temporary, some permanent (e.g. Tristana's Draw a Bead) or conditional; most are lost on death; buffs granted by one champion to another apply the granting champion's magic penetration and damage modifiers; most buffs do not stack with themselves (reapplication only resets duration), a few stack up to N times (e.g. Milio's Warm Hugs up to 2).

name: Buff duration classes
description: The wiki classifies buffs by duration semantics: indefinite (permanent or until consumed), conditionally indefinite (lasts until a condition like taking damage or leaving combat), temporary (fixed duration), and toggled (active form states such as Elise's Spider Form / Human Form).

name: Debuff
description: A status effect that negatively impacts a unit's combat performance; all crowd control counts as a debuff; the wiki categorizes debuffs into statistical, mark-oriented, damage-over-time and damage-modification types; debuffs do not stack with themselves unless stated, and are always temporary or conditional (they do not persist after the target's death).

name: Mark
description: A debuff category whose stacks or presence are meant to be consumed or triggered by subsequent effects: stacking marks with a cap (Braum's Concussive Blows 4, Darius' Hemorrhage 5, Vayne's Silver Bolts 3) that detonate or empower follow-up damage when maxed, and single marks that enable follow-up abilities (Zed's Death Mark, LeBlanc's Sigil of Malice).

name: Damage over time (DoT) debuff
description: A debuff that deals damage in ticks over a duration; several DoTs are stacking (Brand's Blaze up to 3, Twitch's Deadly Venom up to 6, Briar's Crimson Curse up to 5); Nautilus' Titan's Wrath stacks infinitely but individual stacks do not reset the duration.

name: Damage modification debuff
description: Debuffs that alter the damage a target deals or receives (e.g. Amumu's Cursed Touch, Sona's Power Chord - Diminuendo, Vladimir's Hemoplague, Exhaust); includes antiheal/grievous wounds item debuffs and shield-reduction effects.

name: Transform
description: A champion switches between two or more distinct forms with separate abilities, statistics and sometimes portraits (Elise Spider/Human, Jayce Mercury Hammer/Cannon, Nidalee Cougar, Gnar Mini/Mega, Bel'Veth True Form, K'Sante All Out); the wiki tags these champions under the Shapeshifter champion category. Also covers disguise passives (Neeko Inherent Glamour) and level-gated forms (Kayle Divine Ascension).

name: Resource-gated transformation
description: A transformation gated by a resource: the resource builds in combat and at maximum forces (Gnar's Rage Gene transforms him into Mega Gnar, then depletes over time to transform back) or permits (Shyvana's Dragon's Descent) the form change.

name: Toggled form
description: Form-switching abilities that act as a toggle with no duration: Elise's Spider Form / Human Form, Jayce's Transform Mercury Hammer/Cannon, Jinx's Switcheroo!, Rek'Sai's Burrow/Unburrow.

name: Ranged/melee reclassification on transform
description: Transforming changes the champion's ranged/melee classification, altering which items and effects apply; Gnar, Elise, Nidalee, Jayce and Kayle are the only champions conditionally considered both ranged and melee (e.g. Mega Gnar becomes melee).

name: Pet (champion summoned unit)
description: An AI-controlled unit summoned by a champion to assist on the battlefield; pets are a type of champion summoned unit, can be controllable (owner inputs commands, e.g. Ivern's Daisy), uncontrollable (static, e.g. Illaoi's tentacles) or self-controlled (instinct-driven, e.g. Kalista's Sentinel); damage dealt by pets is credited to the summoning champion.

name: Leash / control range
description: A radius relative to the pet's source that the pet cannot physically pass; at max leash range the pet usually blinks back to the caster's location (e.g. Tibbers, Heimerdinger turrets, Illaoi tentacles, Daisy, LeBlanc clone, Orianna ball, Shaco clone, Zed shadow).

name: Clone
description: A copy of a champion that counts as a champion for targeting and most non-takedown interactions but otherwise behaves as a pet; clones inherit item stats and some buffs, their basic attacks do not trigger spell effects, and takedowns scored by clones are attributed to their owner; clones may be controllable (LeBlanc, Shaco, Wukong, Neeko) or uncontrollable.

name: Summoned minion
description: A champion-created minion with its own independent health and stats that exists for a limited time or while the summoner is nearby; damage dealt is credited to the summoning champion and may scale with the summoner's stats; most behave autonomously, some are player-controllable (Tibbers, Daisy).

name: Trap
description: An autonomous unit that is triggered when valid targets enter its trigger range; traps enter stealth after a brief arm time, are revealed by control wards / sweepers, and their damage is classified as ability damage credited to the champion; traps can be targetable (Jhin, Nidalee, Shaco, Teemo) or non-targetable (Caitlyn, Jinx, Maokai, Elise, Bard, Zac).

name: Summoned terrain and structures
description: Player-created terrain units that block movement (Anivia's Crystallize, Jarvan's Cataclysm, Trundle's Pillar of Ice, Yorick's Dark Procession) and champion-summoned structures such as Azir's Sun Disc turret; terrain usually cannot be targeted directly except in special cases.

name: Ward unit
description: A summoner- or item-created unit that grants sight and is a valid target for some effects (Lee Sin's Safeguard, Teleport) but invalid for most others; classified separately from minions, monsters and champions (Stealth Ward, Control Ward, Farsight Ward).

name: Ability resource
description: A tangible resource shown on the champion's health bar that limits or empowers gameplay by being consumed or generated through ability casting and basic attacking; each champion has at most two resources - a primary one (resource line) and a secondary one (pips or champion-specific icons).

name: Mana
description: The primary casting resource of most champions: a blue bar under the health bar; abilities expend mana costs, the pool refills slowly via mana regeneration and can be restored actively; maximum mana = base + bonus mana; mana stacks additively (1:1) and can scale ability/item effects (Muramana, Kassadin Riftwalk, Ryze).

name: Energy
description: An alternative casting resource shown as a yellow bar: regenerates much faster than mana but has a small fixed pool (base 200; Shen 400) that cannot be improved through growth; ultimates cost no energy; the only buff that increases energy regeneration is Crest of Insight.

name: Manaless
description: A champion that does not use nor benefit from mana or mana regeneration (28 champions); manaless champions either use an alternative resource (energy, fury, ferocity, heat, etc.), use the secondary bar as a duration indicator, or have no resource at all.

name: Resourceless
description: A champion with no primary or secondary resource bar at all (Garen, Katarina, Riven, Viego, Dr. Mundo, Zac); internal engine resource index = 2 (none).

name: Fury / Rage resource family
description: An umbrella of champion-specific momentum resources generated in combat (often decaying out of combat) that gate an empowerment or transformation: Gnar's Rage (gnarfury), Renekton's Rage (rage), Rek'Sai's Fury, Sett's Grit, Shyvana's Dragon Fury (dragonfury), Kled's Courage, Tryndamere's Battle Fury (battlefury), Udyr's Awakening, Vladimir's Crimson Rush, Zaahen's Cultivation of War.

name: Heat (overheat)
description: Rumble's resource (internal index 7): casting basic abilities generates heat, which decays when not casting; above a threshold his basic abilities are empowered, and at maximum he overheats - losing heat rapidly while abilities are disabled and basic attacks are enhanced.

name: Ferocity
description: Rengar's resource (internal index 9): generated by casting basic abilities successfully, lost after being out of combat; at maximum, his next basic ability consumes all of it to become empowered; shown as pips that turn orange at max.

name: Blood Well
description: A resource (internal index 10) that thematically drains life force, generated through a champion's empowered form and depleting at a set rate: Aatrox's World Ender, Swain's Demonic Ascension (as Demonic Energy), and Sylas when hijacking those ultimates.

name: Flow
description: Yasuo's and Yone's resource (internal index 11, 'wind'): generated while moving; at maximum it is consumed and converted into a shield upon taking damage from champions or monsters.

name: Ammo / stocked charges
description: A resource (internal index 12) consumed by specific actions, shown as pips or icons below the health bar: basic-attack ammo with reload (Graves, Jhin, Xayah, Gwen), stocked ability casts (Ahri's Spirit Rush, Gangplank's Powder Keg, Syndra's Dark Sphere), and readiness indicators (Annie's Pyromania stun, Pantheon empowered cast, Ryze runes).

name: Moonlight
description: Aphelios' exclusive resource (internal index 13) functioning as ammunition for each of his weapons: the bar is divided into five parts of 10 ammo, expended by basic attacks and his weapon active; a weapon with no moonlight goes to the reserve and is replenished when gained again.

name: Health as a casting resource
description: Certain champions expend a set quantity or percentage of their health to cast some or all abilities, either instead of or in addition to an ability resource; some resourceless champions (Vladimir, Mordekaiser, Zac, etc.) have health costs.

name: Secondary bar as duration indicator
description: The secondary resource bar is used to count down the remaining duration of an ability or state instead of a spendable pool: Aatrox's World Ender (Blood Well in seconds), Bel'Veth's Endless Banquet (True Form), Briar's Blood Frenzy (Frenzy), K'Sante's All Out and Karthus' Death Defied (mana bar), Yone's Soul Unbound (Flow in centiseconds).

name: Internal (engine) resource types
description: Riot's internal resource type indices as documented by the wiki: 0 mana, 1 energy, 2 none, 3 shield (Mordekaiser), 4 battlefury (Tryndamere), 5 dragonfury (Briar/Shyvana/Vex), 6 rage (Renekton), 7 heat (Rumble/Samira), 8 gnarfury (Gnar/Rek'Sai/Sett/Kled/Udyr/Vladimir), 9 ferocity (Rengar), 10 bloodwell (Aatrox/Swain/Sylas), 11 wind (Yasuo/Yone), 12 ammo, 13 moonlight (Aphelios), 14 other.

name: Soul (stack currency)
description: A stack currency collected from takedowns/deaths (Senna Mist, Thresh souls) that permanently scales a stat.
